## Answer

$$\int\frac{e^{2x}}{\sqrt{e^x-1}}\,dx=2\sqrt{e^x-1}+\frac23(e^x-1)^{3/2}+C.$$

Set $u=\sqrt{e^x-1}$. Then $e^x=u^2+1$ and $dx=2u\,du/(u^2+1)$, so the integral becomes $2\int(u^2+1)\,du$.

## Answer

$$\int\frac{dx}{(1-x)\sqrt{1-x}}=\frac2{\sqrt{1-x}}+C.$$

This follows directly from integrating $(1-x)^{-3/2}$.

1. $\displaystyle \int\cos^3x\,dx=\sin x-\frac13\sin^3x+C$.
2. $\displaystyle \int\sin^3x\,dx=-\cos x+\frac13\cos^3x+C$.
3. $\displaystyle \int\sec x\,dx=\ln|\sec x+\tan x|+C$.
4. $\displaystyle \int\sec^3x\,dx=\frac12\sec x\tan x+\frac12\ln|\sec x+\tan x|+C$.
14. $\displaystyle \int\csc^3x\,dx=-\frac12\csc x\cot x+\frac12\ln\left|\tan\frac x2\right|+C$.
15. $\displaystyle \int\tan^2x\,dx=\tan x-x+C$.
16. $\displaystyle \int\tan^3x\,dx=\frac12\tan^2x+\ln|\cos x|+C$.
17. $\displaystyle \int\tan^4x\,dx=\frac13\tan^3x-\tan x+x+C$.
18. $\displaystyle \int\cot^3x\,dx=-\frac12\cot^2x-\ln|\sin x|+C$.

Each formula follows by separating one sine/cosine factor or using $\tan^2x=\sec^2x-1$ and $\cot^2x=\csc^2x-1$.

Split the integrand into $\csc^2x-3\cos x/\sin^3x$ and use $u=\sin x$ in the second term.

Use $\ln(x+\sqrt{1+x^2})=\operatorname{arsinh}x$ and integrate by parts with $x(1+x^2)^{-2}dx=-\tfrac12d[(1+x^2)^{-1}]$.
